sections.h2: What the clerk does with your deed
sections.html:
The clerk records the deed, and that filing is what makes a Louisiana sale effective against everyone outside the contract. Under Civil Code article 3338, a written transfer of land has no effect on third persons until it is recorded in the conveyance records.

The Lafayette Parish clerk serves the 15th Judicial District and acts as ex-officio recorder. The Recording Department files conveyance, mortgage and UCC documents. Each document gets an entry number with the date, hour and minute of filing, and a short description with the first parties shows up on the online records search right away. Between two and three hundred documents come in daily, and full indexing of all party names is done by the next day.

Office: 800 S. Buchanan St., Lafayette, LA 70501. Mail: P.O. Box 2009, Lafayette, LA 70502. Main number (337) 291-6400, Recording Department (337) 291-6310.

A conveyance or mortgage of one to five pages costs $105 to record in a single index type. Every price below already includes the $5 statewide portal fee, indexing of up to ten names and one certified copy.

Document lengthOne book (conveyance or mortgage)Both books
1 to 5 pages$105$205
6 to 25 pages$205$405
26 to 50 pages$305$605
51 pages or more$305 plus $5 per extra page$605 plus $5 per extra page

Use the two-book column when a single document goes into both records. Fees are charged for each book, except that the $5 portal charge applies once. Extras: $5 for each name after the tenth, $20 per page for paper other than 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches, and $25 per debtor on a judgment with no Social Security or tax ID number.

sections.h2: A new recording charge starts in 2027
sections.html:
Act 446 of the 2026 Regular Legislative Session adds $5 to every recorded document, effective January 1, 2027. A closing in late December 2026 and one in early January 2027 can therefore show different recording totals.

The existing $5 portal fee comes from Act 173 of 2017 and took effect August 1, 2018. It pays for the Louisiana Clerks Remote Access Authority, a state entity that runs a statewide portal for remote access to parish land records. Both charges are on top of the page-based fee, so get the total from the closing office before closing day.

Smaller line items appear around the main recording fee:

  • Cancellation or partial release of a single mortgage, lien or privilege: $55.
  • Cancellation with the original paraphed note: $15.
  • Real estate mortgage certificate: $20 for the first name, $10 for each additional name, and $15 for each additional property.
  • Non-lien certificate: $20 per name.
  • Copies: $1 per page in the office, $10 plus the copy fee for a certified copy, and $5 plus the copy fee for a conformed copy.

A mortgage certificate lists the recorded mortgages and privileges against a seller's name. Title agents order one so every lien is confirmed paid and cancelled before the buyer's money is released. The fee schedule has no transfer tax line, so ask your closing agent for the full settlement figures.

sections.h2: How to prepare and submit documents
sections.html:
Each document needs a caption on its first page naming the type of act. Leave a 2 inch margin at the top and 1 inch at the bottom and sides, and use type no smaller than 8 point. Paper can be 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches. These rules come from R.S. 13:844(B).

All pages presented together count as one document, including exhibits, riders, powers of attorney, property descriptions, tax certificates, surveys and mortgage certificates. The count sets the price tier.

The clerk prefers electronic recording and links three e-recording platforms from its home page: CSC, ePN and Simplifile. Most title companies already use one. If you mail a paper act, enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope or pay postage at actual cost.

Unlike in most states, originals sent to the Clerk of the District Court and Ex-Officio Recorder stay in the parish archives. You can get a certified copy instead, either when you file, from the Recording Department, or later, from the Land Records and Copy Department. Order that copy during closing if the Assessor or a lender will want proof of the sale.

Cancellations take a separate route. They go first to the Cancellation Clerk in the Recording Department for verification, and in Lafayette Parish they must be in authentic form, signed by the affiant before a notary public. UCC terminations use a Louisiana-approved form and can be sent directly.

The clerk's online search covers mortgage, conveyance and UCC records. The free eClerks LA portal indexes land, civil, marriage and probate records across Louisiana, and a free alert service there watches land records in other parishes.

Paid access with document images is sold by subscription: $20 for one day, $50 for 30 days or $600 for 365 days, plus $1 per page to print. Searching liens under your name before you list can turn up a forgotten mortgage or judgment that would otherwise surface at closing.

Filings may become public record under the Public Records Act. The courthouse bars cellphones, cameras and recording devices, so bring paper documents and a printed list of the numbers you need.

Here is the usual path for a Lafayette Parish sale. You sign the act of sale at closing. The title company or closing attorney submits it, ideally through one of the e-recording platforms. The Recording Department stamps it with the entry number, date, hour and minute, and the online search shows a short description soon after. Full indexing is done the next day.

If an old mortgage is being paid off, its cancellation travels the same road, through the Cancellation Clerk first. Once the act is recorded, ask for the certified copy. Keep it with your closing papers, since originals are not returned.

sections.h2: Checklist before the deed is recorded
sections.html:
Louisiana lets any party to a conveyance of real property outside New Orleans get a certificate showing whether state, parish, municipal and levee district taxes are paid, other than those for the year of the sale (R.S. 9:2901).

  • Ask for the tax certificate and for a mortgage certificate on every owner's name.
  • Make sure any prior mortgage has a cancellation ready to record.
  • Ask the closing office whether the recording date falls before or after January 1, 2027.
  • Request a certified copy of the recorded act for your own file.

A seller taking a cash offer should run the same list, since the buyer's title agent will do these searches before funding. Problems are cheaper to fix before closing day.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Lafayette Parish?
faqs.a: A one to five page conveyance in a single book costs $105, which includes a $5 portal fee, ten indexed names and one certified copy. Six to 25 pages costs $205.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax on the Lafayette Parish fee schedule?
faqs.a: The schedule lists recording, cancellation, copy and certificate fees but no transfer tax line. Ask your closing agent for the full settlement figures.

faqs.q: Does the Lafayette Parish clerk return my original deed?
faqs.a: No. Originals become part of the parish archives. You can get a certified copy at filing or later from the Land Records and Copy Department.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in Lafayette Parish?
faqs.a: Yes, and the clerk encourages it. The clerk's site links to CSC, ePN and Simplifile for electronic recording of mortgage, conveyance and UCC documents.
Act 446 of the 2026 Regular Legislative Session adds $5 to every recorded document starting that date.
